analysis:
All four changed files are CI/automation workflows and touch no provider runtime, key, attestation, cache or wire-protocol code. None of the retained threat entries (T-041, TB-011 and the others) is affected.

ci-master.yml: pull_request now also fires on `labeled`. The macOS provider and cluster `tests` job runs on PRs only when the `run-ci` or `run-gpu-ci` label is present, and always on pushes. Only users with triage or write access can add labels, so this narrows automatic execution of PR code on macOS runners. The new `unlabel` job holds `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` on the `pull_request` event, not `pull_request_target`. Fork PRs therefore get a read-only token and no secrets, so the DELETEs fail harmlessly (`|| true`). The label name and PR number are passed through env vars, not interpolated into the script, so there is no injection. The concurrency group isolates unrelated labels so they cannot cancel a `run-ci` run. The path-bypass risk is low: Release Integrity and Docs Lint still run on every event type. Not verifiable here: `provider-plan.yml` and `provider-tests.yml` were not supplied, so the new `run_tests` input and `cluster_gpu` output are unconfirmed. A mismatch would be a CI failure, not a security issue.

claude.yml and codex.yml: the Blacksmith runner became GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`, and `timeout-minutes` was added (30 and 5). Triggers, permissions, secrets and action pins are unchanged. The timeouts reduce runaway-job exposure. The pre-existing `contents: write`/`id-token: write` grants on comment-triggered runs are out of scope.

darkbloom-route.yml: adds a `max-attempts` input, validated with `^[1-9]$`, passed via env, and used in a bounded retry loop. The loop has a 140s ceiling and 5s per attempt. It parses Retry-After strictly (a single numeric header, at most 5 digits, at most 86400, then clamped to 15s). The server error body is reduced to an allowlisted code before logging. `configuration_error` strips newlines and `%` and truncates to 200 characters, which prevents workflow-command injection. Header and body temp files are cleaned up by the trap. Fallback and routing semantics outside the shown hunks are not visible, so the next pass should confirm the loop's exit path still reaches the same fallback handling.
